title: Two-step token bit encoding
statement: Let $x,p,r$ be Boolean words and $b$ a Boolean, with $x=pbr$. Starting in the token-scanning state at the position immediately after $p$, with prior output $o$, after two steps the encoder is at the position immediately after $pb$ and has appended $bb$ to its output. Its state is the token-scanning state if $b$ is true and the separator-phase state if $b$ is false.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is the concatenation of $p$, the bit $b$, and $r$
The initial scan position is $|p|$ and is within the input
replaced:
If the input splits as $x = p\, b\, r$ with bit $b$, two transitions of the
token encoder from its scanning state at position $\abs{p}$ emit $b$ twice
and advance the input head once; the encoder continues token scanning when
$b = 1$ and passes to the separator phase when $b = 0$.
